entradas.text: I had been invited to an exclusive preview of Alfred Kcirbuk's new film, "The Morning Shall Come".

With its massive budget and Kcirbuk's directorial cachet, this drama was set to be a milestone for Sordland's burgeoning film scene. Personally, though, I was just looking forward to spending some time with my family.
It was a very hot and sunny day as Serge drove us to the old capital. The film was to be screened in the historic Cinema Anglei dei Erlory -- the very first cinema in Sordland.
Serge had maxed out the air conditioning to keep the Kadilla comfortable. I kept silent through most of our ride on the H-1. I couldn't get my mind off the results of the Assembly vote.
I gazed at the vast plains between Holsord and Erlory as we drove on the H-1. Serge had maxed out the air conditioning to keep the Kadilla comfortable.
"Look what you've done, Deana..."
Deana looked down.
"Anton! For God's sake!"
"If you were going to bring your work stress into this, you shouldn't have taken us along."
"If you were going to bring your work stress into this, you shouldn't have taken us along."
"All she wanted to do was cheer you up."
"True. Next time you'll stay home."
entradas.menu: "True. Next time you'll stay home."

entradas.text: "I know, I know. I didn't mean to make her sad..."
entradas.menu: "I know, I know. I didn't mean to make her sad..."

entradas.text: "You are right. I'm sorry for lashing out."
entradas.menu: "You are right. I am sorry..."

entradas.text: "Not again..."
Besides which, Petr had worked hard with the producers to make this screening possible during the emergency, albeit with limited attendance and heavy security.
Serge rolled down the soundproof glass between us.
"Relax! I was just joking..."
entradas.menu: "Relax! I was just joking..."

entradas.text: "How very presidential of you, making decisions on behalf of the rest of us."
"Just watch your tone with the kids, Anton. Please control your stress."
"Really? You were *joking*?"
"It's okay. But please watch your tone with the kids, Anton."
Franc turned toward us for the first time since he'd gotten in the car.
"Sir, we are about to enter Erlory. We'll be at the cinema in a few minutes."
"Thank you, Serge."
entradas.menu: "Thank you, Serge."

entradas.text: "Finally."
entradas.menu: "Finally."

entradas.text: "Good. Thanks for telling me."
entradas.menu: "Good. Thanks for telling me."

entradas.text: "Is there something wrong, sir?"
"My dad's just sick of us, Serge."
I took a brief look outside as Serge rolled the soundproof glass up again.
I could see the many towers of Erlory rising over what was left of the old city walls.
I could see the many towers of Erlory rising over what was left of the old city walls.
In the distance, there were several planes flying towards the city.
As they got closer to us, I saw that they were military planes that looked like the sharp-edged Arcasian designs. They were probably headed for our new joint military base.
"Hah, young sir, don't say that. Why would Mr. President get sick of you? He loves you all more than anything."
"Don't mind him, Serge."
entradas.menu: "Don't mind him, Serge."

entradas.text: "Franc, enough. Could you roll the glass up again, Serge?"
entradas.menu: "Franc, enough. Could you roll the glass up again, Serge?"

entradas.text: "Serge is right."
entradas.menu: "Serge is right."

entradas.text: "Of course, sir."
"Oh, sir, I don't mind the young mister. He's an intelligent young man."
"It's true!"
Franc rolled his eyes.
"Wasn't your vineyard around here?"
"At any rate, we'll be there in a minute. I'll leave you to it for now."
Monica pointed at the hills on the outskirts of the city.
"It's not mine. It's ours."
entradas.menu: "It's not mine. It's ours."

entradas.text: "It's just behind those hills. We should go there sometime."
entradas.menu: "It's just behind those hills. We should go there sometime."

entradas.text: "Yes. It's already started producing wine again, too. We'll have our own wine soon!"
entradas.menu: "Yes. It's already started producing wine again, too. We'll have our own wine soon!"

entradas.text: "Rayne Wines! Made by a family who knows nothing about making wine!"
"That would be lovely."
She smiled.
She did not respond.
"Speak for yourself, Franc."
entradas.menu: "Speak for yourself, Franc."

entradas.text: "Doesn't sound half bad, actually."
entradas.menu: "Doesn't sound half bad, actually."

entradas.text: "We're not the ones making the wine, genius."
entradas.menu: "We're not the ones making the wine, genius."

entradas.text: "I know. Why lie? The truth always sounds better anyway."
"I meant 'Rayne Wines,' but sure."
entradas.menu: "I meant 'Rayne Wines,' but sure."

entradas.text: "Are you sure about that, son? Truth doesn't really sell."
entradas.menu: "Are you sure about that, son? Truth doesn't really sell."

entradas.text: "Okay, Franc..."
entradas.menu: "Okay, Franc..."

entradas.text: "Yeah, okay. I know that my grandfather used to be a wine connoisseur or something. But did you really learn how to make wine?"
"I'm sorry. I guess you know everything, dad."
"If only everyone thought like that, son..."
entradas.menu: "If only everyone thought like that, son..."

entradas.text: Serge knocked on the glass and gestured forwards.
She did not respond.
We were at the main square of Erlory, and the historic 'Cinema Anglei'—the Cinema of Angels—was right in front of us.
"Is this the place?"
"Yeah."
Franc fidgeted with his tie as he stared out the window.
"Come on. Let's get out."
It was an old baroque-style corner building with walls that looked like marble from a distance. There were exquisite ornaments on each side of every window.
Serge pulled the car to the entrance of the building, which was lit by vivid neon stripes in many colors.
Serge opened the doors, and we exited onto the red carpet.
In contrast with the cinema's baroque-style exterior, the inside was modern and sleek, with bare walls painted in black, red and white.
The film's cast and crew were already in the foyer, with glasses of champagne in their hands.
Serge opened the doors, and we exited onto the red carpet.
As they noticed us and our many guards, the mood in the room immediately soured.
We approached the crowd and were welcomed by the producers and the event organizers.
On the wall next to the entrance, there were painted the words "Stop The Oppression of Bluds".
On the wall next to the entrance, there were painted the words "Stop The Oppression of Bluds".
Other graffiti next to it read, "Stop the Genocide in Wehlen" and "Axis of Evil: Smolak, Rayne, Lancea."
As the police escorted us inside the cinema, a journalist broke through our security cordon and started running at me.
As soon as he yelled "Mr. President!" one of the policemen kicked him in the back and forced him down onto the ground. Another grabbed me by the suit jacket and quickly ushered me away.
He motioned for me and my family to continue along the security corridor.
"Was that strictly necessary?"
entradas.menu: "Was that strictly necessary?"

entradas.text: "Excuse us, Mr. President."
I followed along, silently.
entradas.menu: Follow along.

entradas.text: "Don't touch me again."
entradas.menu: "Don't touch me again."

entradas.text: A man walked up to us with quick steps.
"Everything is for your safety, sir."
"We had to for your safety, sir."
He and the other guards seemed not to care what had just happened. We kept walking through the corridor.
We were just about to enter the building when a journalist managed to block the path.
"Mr. President! Mr. President!"
"Madame! Mr. President! It's so good to see you here."
"Why don't we take our seats? It's about to start."
He gently bowed at Monica and shook our hands.
"It's an honor to meet you. I'm Alfred Kcirbuk."
"Nice to meet you, Mr. Kcirbuk."
entradas.menu: "Nice to meet you, Mr. Kcirbuk."

entradas.text: "The honor is mine, Mr. Kcirbuk. I'm a big fan of your work."
entradas.menu: "The honor is mine, Mr. Kcirbuk. I'm a big fan of your work."

entradas.text: "It's very humbling to know that you've been watching and enjoying my movies."
Franc snorted. I glanced at him, and he innocently took a sip of his cola.
"If you don't mind my asking, which one was your favorite? This one may be slightly different than my previous works."
"I loved The Sordish Dream."
entradas.menu: "I loved The Sordish Dream."

entradas.text: "All of them are my favourites, Mr. Kcirbuk."
entradas.menu: "All of them are my favourites, Mr. Kcirbuk."

entradas.text: "I loved The Man Who Saved The World."
entradas.menu: "I loved The Man Who Saved The World."

entradas.text: He stared at me for a while as if he was trying to understand if I was joking or not.
"You flatter me too much, Mr. President. I myself know they aren't all winners."
He laughed.
"Come now, just pick one!"
"That's by Mikel Vargas, Mr. President. It beat my film The Sordish Dream for the top prize at the Benfi Festival last year."
"Oh, really? Then you might enjoy this one too."
"I'll admit, I didn't expect you to be such a cinephile."
Franc looked me in the eye and struggled not to laugh.
Although I wasn't in much of a moviegoing mood, it would have been unpresidential not to attend.
"Worried about the university exams, son?"
entradas.menu: "Worried about the university exams, son?"

entradas.text: "What's wrong, Franc?"
entradas.menu: "What's wrong, Franc?"

entradas.text: I ignored him and turned to Deana.
entradas.menu: Ignore him and talk to Deana.

entradas.text: "Since when do you care what's happening in my life?"
Serge had maxed out the air conditioning to keep the Kadilla comfortable. But that wasn't the only reason I felt a chill in the air.
"Never mind."
entradas.menu: "Never mind."

entradas.text: "I've been busy lately, but I'll always have time for you."
entradas.menu: "I've been busy lately, but I'll always have time for you."

entradas.text: "You know I'll support you whether you pass or fail those exams."
entradas.menu: "You know I'll support you whether you pass or fail those exams."

entradas.text: I noticed Franc fidgeting with his tie anxiously.
I turned to Deana.
"Excited for the movie?"
entradas.menu: "Excited for the movie, sweetie?"

entradas.text: "Busy with failure?"
"Franc, don't talk to your father that way! He tried his best."
"What an honor, Your Highness."
Monica suppressed a smirk.
"Franc, don't talk to your father that way! He's been working so hard for this country."
"Are you having a good time, sweetie?"
entradas.menu: "Are you having a good time, sweetie?"

entradas.text: "Are you in a better mood than your brother?"
entradas.menu: "Are you in a better mood than your brother?"

entradas.text: Deana nodded shyly and hugged her stuffed animal closer to her chest. Monica draped a protective arm around her. Nobody spoke for the rest of the ride.
Deana nodded happily.
"Hah! I won't lose. Isn't that right, Monica?"
entradas.menu: "Hah! I won't lose. Isn't that right, Monica?"

entradas.text: "What about you, Papa? You won something, right? You should smile! And keep doing your best even if you lose."
"I'm just fine, Deana. Everything's going to be wonderful from now on, right, Monica?"
entradas.menu: "I'm just fine, Deana. Everything's going to be wonderful from now on, right, Monica?"

entradas.text: "That's my girl. Thanks a lot."
entradas.menu: "That's my girl. Thanks a lot."

entradas.text: "Don't worry about me, Papa! You've got the whole country to worry about!"
"What about you, Papa? I know you're sad, but failure helps us grow, right?"
"Exactly! Now, where did you learn that?"
entradas.menu: "Exactly! Now, where did you learn that?"

entradas.text: "All I'm worried about is whether or not there will be popcorn."
entradas.menu: "All I'm worried about is whether or not there will be popcorn."

entradas.text: "Ugh. Thanks for the reminder."
entradas.menu: "Ugh. Thanks for the reminder."

entradas.text: "From you!"
Deana giggled.
"I sure hope so."
Deana giggled.
"How should I know? I don't meddle in these affairs."
"Everything's going to be wonderful from now on, isn't it, Monica?"
entradas.menu: "Everything's going to be wonderful from now on, isn't it, Monica?"

entradas.text: "Now, no more politics talk! Isn't that right, Monica?"
entradas.menu: "Now, no more politics talk! Isn't that right, Monica?"

entradas.text: "You've been awfully quiet, Monica."
entradas.menu: "You've been awfully quiet, Monica."

entradas.text: "Of course. Let's just focus on having a nice time at the movies."
"Oh, you've made sure of that."
"I just want to focus on having a nice time at the movies."
"Don't take that tone with me! You don't know the stress I'm under."
entradas.menu: "Don't take that tone with me! You don't know the stress I'm under."

entradas.text: I said nothing. We drove on in silence.
entradas.menu: Say nothing.

entradas.text: "Anton you can't act like this with us. I'm not your assistant."
"Darling, we've been through this. I'm sorry."
entradas.menu: "Darling, we've been through this. I'm sorry."

entradas.text: Monica folded her arms. We drove on in silence.
"Great! We will!"
"Who?"
entradas.menu: "Who?"

entradas.text: "The... the director of tonight's film. I was told you were a big fan of my work."
"My producers told me you had expressed admiration for my work."
We entered the screening room, the lights dimmed, and the film began.
It was a period drama set in the 1870s, about a Sordish soldier who pursues a doomed romance with a widowed Bludish farmer during the conquest of Bergia.
I wondered briefly whether Kcirbuk was commenting on my own treatment of the Bludish people. But then, he had finished filming long before I became president.
As the credits rolled, I made an early exit to use the men's room. I was washing my hands when I heard an unmistakeable voice behind me.
"So, what did you think?"

Tarquin Soll leaned on his cane. He had aged noticeably since the last time I saw him, his appearance far more frail. Yet beneath it all, I could still sense the raw magnetism that had kept him in power for 20 years.
Tarquin Soll leaned on his cane. He had the same frail appearance I'd noticed at the Assembly meeting. Yet up close, I could still sense the raw magnetism that had kept him in power for 20 years.
"Complete and utter drivel. What about yourself?"
entradas.menu: "Complete and utter drivel. What about yourself?"

entradas.text: "Dangerous pro-Bludish propaganda. I ought to have it banned."
entradas.menu: "Dangerous pro-Bludish propaganda. I ought to have it banned."

entradas.text: "I'm happy the plight of the Bludish might finally get the attention it deserves."
entradas.menu: "I'm happy the plight of the Bludish might finally get the attention it deserves."

entradas.text: "I found the plot questionable, but it certainly looked spectacular. What about yourself?"
entradas.menu: "I found the plot questionable, but it certainly looked spectacular. What about yourself?"

entradas.text: "Sentimental pablum for the enjoyment of housewives only. And for a period piece, the script contained far too many anachronisms."
"Indubitably."
entradas.menu: "Indubitably."

entradas.text: "Totes."
entradas.menu: "Totes."

entradas.text: "Not an unwise decision, President Rayne."
"Be careful where you extend your sympathies, President Rayne."
"What the hell are you doing here, Mr. Soll?"
entradas.menu: "What the hell are you doing here, Mr. Soll?"

entradas.text: "What the hell were you doing at the Assembly vote, Mr. Soll?"
entradas.menu: "What the hell were you doing at the Assembly vote, Mr. Soll?"

entradas.text: "Enough small talk. What brought you here from your island?"
entradas.menu: "Enough small talk. What brought you here from your island?"

entradas.text: "Enough small talk. Why were you at the Assembly vote?"
entradas.menu: "Enough small talk. Why were you at the Assembly vote?"

entradas.text: "A man's got to get off his island every once in a while, you know."
He smiled, but I could see no mirth on his face.
"And I wanted to check in on how my country has been faring in my absence."
"My country was about to make a rash decision. I couldn't simply sit by."
"It's not *your* country anymore."
entradas.menu: "It's not *your* country anymore."

entradas.text: "Your scheme didn't work. I won."
entradas.menu: "Your scheme didn't work. I won."

entradas.text: "You've succeeded, for now. But you won't be able to stop me for long."
entradas.menu: "You've succeeded, for now. But you won't be able to stop me for long."

entradas.text: "I suppose it isn't."
"No?"
There was a glint in his eye.
"Enjoy that power while it lasts."
entradas.menu: "Enjoy that power while it lasts."

entradas.text: "It's not *your* country anymore."
entradas.menu: "It's not *your* country anymore."

entradas.text: "I can handle Sordland without you, old man."
entradas.menu: "I can handle Sordland without you, old man."

entradas.text: "Your presence is appreciated. But I've got everything under control."
entradas.menu: "Your presence is appreciated. But I've got everything under control."

entradas.text: There was a glint in his eye.
"No?"
"Yes, I can see that."
"I wouldn't be so sure about that."
"You may still have your loyalists. But I'm the one in control."
entradas.menu: "You may still have your loyalists. But I'm the one in control."

entradas.text: "I'm happy you're looking out for me. But I don't need any help."
entradas.menu: "I'm happy you're looking out for me. But I don't need any help."

entradas.text: "I was wrong to champion you all those years ago. You proved to be a spineless weasel!"
I stormed past him and out the door.
entradas.menu: Storm out.

entradas.text: "History will show who's what, Colonel."
entradas.menu: "History will show who's what, Colonel."

entradas.text: "You bastard!"
entradas.menu: "You bastard!"

entradas.text: "Now, if you'll excuse me, I've got my garden to get back to. Someone has to keep the weeds from spreading."
"And are you pleased with the outcome?"
entradas.menu: "And are you pleased with the outcome?"

entradas.text: Soll fixed me with a piercing stare. His back straightened.
"Perhaps my clout with the Assembly isn't what it used to be. But you may yet encounter difficulties pushing your reforms through the Supreme Court."
"Threats don't suit you, Anton."
"Quite."
"You won't get away with your meddling."
entradas.menu: "You won't get away with your meddling."

entradas.text: "A true president knows when he must step down."
entradas.menu: "A true president knows when he must step down."

entradas.text: "But why did you block my reforms?"
entradas.menu: "But why did you block my reforms?"

entradas.text: "Why do you want these reforms blocked so badly?"
entradas.menu: "Why do you want these reforms blocked so badly?"

entradas.text: "A true president knows when he must step down."
entradas.menu: "A true president knows when he must step down."

entradas.text: "Your cronies can't help you now."
entradas.menu: "Your cronies can't help you now."

entradas.text: "I will not have my party and my Constitution tarnished by a tyrant."
"I will not let you and that bleeding-heart idiot Ricter tarnish my precious Constitution."
"I will not let an upstart like you tarnish my party and my Constitution."
"A lesson you'd be wise to learn yourself."
"Ricter's a better man than you ever were."
entradas.menu: "Ricter's a better man than you ever were."

entradas.text: "Your Constitution is ancient history. My reforms will bring Sordland into the future."
entradas.menu: "Your Constitution is ancient history. My reforms will bring Sordland into the future."

entradas.text: "Ha!"
Some of his spittle landed on my cheek.
"You tarnished it enough for the both of us already."
entradas.menu: "You tarnished it enough for the both of us already."

entradas.text: "I'm doing this for the good of the country."
entradas.menu: "I'm doing this for the good of the country."

entradas.text: "Ha!"
Some of his spittle landed on my cheek.
"I saw right through Ricter in the '30s, and he hasn't changed a bit. That man will do and say anything to advance his own cause."
Some of his spittle landed on my cheek.
"Ha!"
"Ha!"
Some of his spittle landed on my cheek.
"Sounds familiar."
entradas.menu: "Sounds familiar."

entradas.text: "If Sordland remains in your hands, the only future I see is anarchy."
"I know, but I need him on my side to undo your damage."
entradas.menu: "I know, but I need him on my side to undo your damage."

entradas.text: "You're wrong about him."
entradas.menu: "You're wrong about him."

entradas.text: "I'm fully aware of your intention to punish me for some crime you think I committed. As if you, Anton Rayne, are above it all. As if you're capable of remaining president without getting your hands dirty."
"As if you, Anton Rayne, are above it all. As if you're capable of remaining president without getting your hands dirty."
"I'll see you punished yet."
entradas.menu: "I'll see you punished yet."

entradas.text: "I am."
entradas.menu: "I am."

entradas.text: "I'm no saint. But I'm trying to act for the good of the country."
entradas.menu: "I'm no saint. But I'm trying to act for the good of the country."

entradas.text: "I always looked up to you. Just give me a chance to do my job."
entradas.menu: "I always looked up to you. Just give me a chance to do my job."

entradas.text: "You'll find out soon enough how your country repays you for your 'goodness'."
He slipped past me and out the door.
Soll's security staff and mine were now clustered outside the washroom, forming a buffer against the large crowd that had gathered.
"That's Tarquin Soll!" I heard someone scream. His guards closed around him, and mine around me.
By the time the chaos subsided, I was back in the car with my family, and Soll was long gone.
I stormed past him and out the door.
"I've known it since you opposed me all those years ago. You spineless backstabbing weasel!"
"I've known it since you turned down the position I offered you all those years ago. You spineless weasel!"
"You took the court's advice and extended the state of emergency. Very prudent."
"Thanks, Colonel. Your opinion means a lot."
entradas.menu: "Thanks, Colonel. Your opinion means a lot."

entradas.text: "Anything to keep my enemies at bay."
entradas.menu: "Anything to keep my enemies at bay."

entradas.text: "I'm surprised to see you here, sir."
entradas.menu: "I'm surprised to see you here, sir."

entradas.text: "I'm surprised to see you're still around, sir. What were you doing at the Assembly?"
entradas.menu: "I'm surprised to see you're still around, sir. What were you doing at the Assembly?"

entradas.text: "I'll tell you who I was wrong about: you. You spineless weasel!"
"I'm right about him, the same way I was right never to trust you. You spineless weasel!"
"You have no idea what it takes to do this job, boy. But you'll find out soon enough."
"At last, I can admit it: I never did like you."
entradas.menu: "At last, I can admit it: I never did like you."

entradas.text: "I still have immense respect for you, Colonel. I wish it was reciprocated."
entradas.menu: "I still have immense respect for you, Colonel. I wish it was reciprocated."

entradas.text: "It will be when you prove yourself worthy of it."
"The Assembly considers me worthy. Doesn't that count for anything?"
entradas.menu: "The Assembly considers me worthy. Doesn't that count for anything?"

entradas.text: "If Sordland remains in your hands, the only future I see is misery."
"There's nothing you can do anymore, old man."
entradas.menu: "There's nothing you can do anymore, old man."

entradas.text: "Well-spoken as always. We'll see how well it serves you during your trial."
entradas.menu: "Well-spoken as always. We'll see how well it serves you during your trial."

entradas.text: "You had your chance to lead. Everyone saw what a mess you made of it."
entradas.menu: "You had your chance to lead. Everyone saw what a mess you made of it."

entradas.text: "I wouldn't be so sure about that."
"I can handle Sordland without you, old man."
entradas.menu: "I can handle Sordland without you, old man."

entradas.text: "Banning the Young Sords, while the communists and Bludish scum run rampant?"
"Why did you end the state of emergency so prematurely?"
"Do you see me as your puppet?"
entradas.menu: "Do you see me as your puppet?"

entradas.text: "I see."
entradas.menu: "I see."

entradas.text: "You could have spoken to me directly."
entradas.menu: "You could have spoken to me about it directly."

entradas.text: "The country still needs to be brought out of recession. This was a distraction."
entradas.menu: "The country still needs to be brought out of recession. This was a distraction."

entradas.text: "I judged that the worst of the threat was over."
entradas.menu: "I judged that the worst of the threat was over."

entradas.text: "It was reflecting badly on my reputation as a democratic leader."
entradas.menu: "It was reflecting badly on my reputation as a democratic leader."

entradas.text: "It was a hard decision, but I did what I had to."
entradas.menu: "It was a hard decision, but I did what I had to."

entradas.text: "I wanted to stop the violence. They were the worst offenders."
entradas.menu: "I wanted to stop the violence. They were the worst offenders."

entradas.text: "They had to be punished for Circas' murder."
entradas.menu: "They had to be punished for Circas' murder."

entradas.text: "My decisions are not your business."
entradas.menu: "My decisions are not your business."

entradas.text: "Your decision not to ban the Workers Party of Bludia may cause problems, however. They clearly are a continuation of the Bludish Freedom Front."
"Your decision not to ban the Red Youth may cause problems, however."
"A ban will only lead to further violence."
entradas.menu: "A ban will only lead to further violence."

entradas.text: He heaved a sigh.
"Short-sighted. I tried to warn Hawker about you."
He raised his eyebrows.
"Do you truly believe Hawker came to you of his own accord?"
"What do you mean?"
entradas.menu: "What do you mean?"

entradas.text: "Wait. The emergency declaration was your idea?"
entradas.menu: "Wait. The emergency declaration was your idea?"

entradas.text: "You spoke to Hawker?"
entradas.menu: "You spoke to Hawker?"

entradas.text: "Don't be naive, Anton."
"How do you think I've been spending my retirement? Just tending to my garden in my island?"
"I've got to protect my party and my legacy somehow. Hawker and Graf advise me on how."
"I told Hawker you could be counted on to make the right choice."
"The police are doing enough to keep the Bludish in line."
entradas.menu: "The police are doing enough to keep the Bludish in line."

entradas.text: "The police are already doing enough to keep the communists in line."
entradas.menu: "The police are already doing enough to keep the communists in line."

entradas.text: "The Bludish were your problem, not mine."
entradas.menu: "The Bludish were your problem, not mine."

entradas.text: "The police are already doing enough to keep the communists in line."
entradas.menu: "The communists were your problem, not mine."

entradas.text: He raised his eyebrows.
"Our problems are one and the same. Do you truly believe Hawker came to you of his own accord?"
"And what good would that have done? You haven't trusted me since the Party Congress."
"I always looked up to you. Just give me a chance to do my job."
entradas.menu: "I've always looked up to you. Just give me a chance to do my job."

entradas.text: "You have no idea what it takes to do this job, boy. But you'll find out soon enough."
He slipped past me and out the door.
"I'm happy to hear that."
"Next time, perhaps I will."
"I see you as a novice in need of some valuable guidance."
"You can trust me."
entradas.menu: "You can trust me."

entradas.text: "You had your chance to lead. Everyone saw what a mess you made."
entradas.menu: "You had your chance to lead. Everyone saw what a mess you made."

entradas.text: "I'm warning you, sir. Stay out of my presidency.
entradas.menu: "I'm warning you, sir. Stay out of my presidency."

entradas.text: Soll fixed me with a piercing stare. He was an old man now -- how could he still be so intimidating?
"Tread carefully, Mr. Rayne."
"Your constitutional reforms made it through the Assembly -- how do you feel about their chances with the Supreme Court?"
"How are you handling the defeat of your constitutional reforms in the Assembly?"
"Thank you, Mr. President. And were you aware that Tarquin Soll would be present at the proceedings?"
"You recently rescinded your emergency declaration. Do you feel that the state has achieved its goals?"
"Yes, the threats to the nation have been neutralized."
entradas.menu: "Yes, the threats to the nation have been neutralized."

entradas.text: "Our enemies are still out there. But we cannot keep living in fear."
entradas.menu: "Our enemies are still out there. But we cannot keep living in fear."

entradas.text: "Declaring the emergency was a mistake. The country's back on the right path now."
entradas.menu: "Declaring the emergency was a mistake. The country's back on the right path now."

entradas.text: "One more question. Can you comment on the arrests of Marcel Koronti and Walter Tusk following the state takeovers of their companies?"
"One more question. Can you comment on the arrest of Marcel Koronti following the state takeover of his corporation?"
"One more question. Can you comment on the arrest of Walter Tusk following the state takeover of his corporation?"
"One more question..."
"He got in my way."
entradas.menu: "He got in my way."

entradas.text: "An unfortunate casualty, but nationalization is the only way forward."
entradas.menu: "An unfortunate casualty, but nationalization is the only way forward."

entradas.text: "No, I have no comment."
entradas.menu: "No, I have no comment."

entradas.text: "They got in my way."
entradas.menu: "They got in my way."

entradas.text: "He got in my way."
entradas.menu: "He got in my way."

entradas.text: "I'm going to keep fighting for my changes. This isn't over yet."
entradas.menu: "I'm going to keep fighting for my changes. This isn't over yet."

entradas.text: "I will respect the Assembly's decision."
entradas.menu: "I will respect the Assembly's decision."

entradas.text: "Not very well, to be honest."
entradas.menu: "Not very well, to be honest."

entradas.text: "Of course I was."
entradas.menu: "Of course I was."

entradas.text: "No, I had to find out from my driver."
entradas.menu: "No, I had to find out from my driver."

entradas.text: "I refuse to discuss Colonel Soll at this time."
entradas.menu: "I refuse to discuss Colonel Soll at this time."

entradas.text: "I trust the justices will make the right decision."
entradas.menu: "I trust the justices will make the right decision."

entradas.text: "The court will vote my way if they know what's good for them."
entradas.menu: "The court will vote my way if they know what's good for them."

entradas.text: "One way or another, these reforms will pass."
entradas.menu: "One way or another, these reforms will pass."

entradas.text: Before she could ask anything else, the guards ushered us inside the theater.
"Don't make me angry, Franc."
entradas.menu: "Don't make me angry, Franc."

entradas.text: Franc turned his head away to look outside the window.
"*You* calling me a tyrant, of all people?"
entradas.menu: "*You* calling me a tyrant, of all people?"

entradas.text: "You're hurting me, Franc."
entradas.menu: "You're hurting me, Franc."
